newsitem.title: UK: Unitor sees no significant sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Unitor sees no significant sales growth.

text.p: Norwegian ships' equipment supplier Unitor Ships Service ASA said Thursday it does not expect any significant sales growth in the second half of this year.
The company blamed uncertainty over freight rates in the tanker and dry bulk markets, and worries of overcapacity, for its guarded outlook.
Unitor earlier reported net profit for the first six months of the year fell to Norwegian crowns 45 million from 69 million in the same period a year earlier.
Sales fell to crowns 1.21 billion from 1.48 bln, but the company said the performance was satisfactory under the circumstances.
"In the light of the restructuring process the company has been through, the result is considered satisfactory," Unitor said.
The company said sales of its products are closely linked to market conditions faced by ship owners and operators.

"Uncertainty regarding the rate development in the bulk market, unpredictability in the tank market, and a certain overcapacity in both, makes it somewhat difficult to predict this year's outlook," Unitor said.
"Based on these and other factors, no significant sales growth in expected within Unitors' existing product areas in the second half of 1997."
Unitor added that it was continuing to search for new permanent president following the resignation of Karsten Houm in April after more than 11 years with the company.
Per Terje Norheim is the acting president. -Reuters Shipping News +44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017
